test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 05 Dec 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Right to Freedom of Religion is contained within which Articles of the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 25 to Article 28**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 25 of the Indian constitution guarantees the Right to Freedom of Religion to its citizens.
 
• It provides freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
 
• It is a basic human right guarantee that cannot be subverted or misinterpreted in any manner.
 
• Article 25 to Article 28 of the Indian constitution deals with the Right to Freedom of Religion.
 
• The objective of the Constitutional Right to Freedom of Religion in India is to sustain the principle of secularism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Secularism:

 
• The term secular has been derived from the Latin word ‘seculum’ which means an age, an indefinite period, or the present age.
 
• Secularism in the Indian context means first, ‘Dharmanirapaksata’ or impartiality to religion and secondly, ‘Sarva Dharma Sama Bhava’ or equal respect for all religions based on the principle of accommodation of all religions.
 
• A Secular State does not identify itself with any particular religion but protects and respects all faiths until they become a danger to the unity and integrity of the country.
 
• The most essential factors of secularism were granting equal status to all religions in India.
 
• Indian secularism is a multi-value character and gives importance to moral reasoning and equally respecting all religions.
